minimumSqlite: 3.39.4, built from the fixture checksum-verified official amalgamation
procedure: Use a scratch export; run each file in a fresh HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, LLV_STATE_DIR and TMPDIR, with LLV_VIEWER_CONTROL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1 and LLV_GATE_RUNNER=off.
Build the minimum SQLite library once with minimumSqliteLibrary(); pass its absolute path through LLV_MINIMUM_SQLITE_LIBRARY.

All test campaigns ran sequentially through the pipeline-supplied gate-slot.sh from revision 34b741354731, using --record and wait_for_check. Each raw command receipt and every file log is retained in pipeline evidence.

To reproduce the original race, export the base, overlay the current test and writer fixture, then select the two publication cases. For the timeout diagnostic, release the publisher before asserting its result.
The cleanup failure control uses the atomic-ticket implementation with the original cleanup stat call; the controlled ordering then produces ENOENT.

cause.ciObservation: The reported CI case had one successful writer and two quota refusals instead of three, lasting 5459.45 ms. Its child stderr was not collected.
cause.controlledObservation: A queue scanner can unlink an empty or partial owner ticket after file creation and before writeFileSync finishes. The live writer resumes without a ticket and times out after its existing five-second lock budget.
cause.attribution: The controlled original-source failure reproduces the CI exit-count and duration signature. The failing path uses filesystem locks; the minimum-SQLite preload does not propagate into writer children.
cause.fix: Write complete owner JSON to a private partial and atomically rename it into the queue. Startup cleanup tolerates a partial disappearing during publication; aged crash debris remains reclaimable.
cause.unchangedAssertions: Four distinct 4 MiB writers still require exactly one success and three quota refusals, and total stored bytes must stay within the original cap. No quota or lock deadline was increased.

writePath.reader: readOwnerFile plus the sorted live-ticket scan
cleanup: writer finally removes its staging file and ticket
writePath.defaults: Production callers retain the existing five-second wait; deputyCommand retains its explicit zero wait.
